afraa, aasa and iata leaders said they support api and pnr data transfer but stressed alignment with internationally recognised standards and correct funding.
iata represents over 370 airlines accounting for about 85% of global air traffic.
iata, afraa and aasa jointly urged african states to implement api and pnr systems in accordance with icao standards and global best practices.
the organisations urged governments not to fund api and pnr programmes through charges on airlines or passengers.

aeroshark uses microscopic grooves 50 micrometers high to reduce aerodynamic drag, saving approximately 1% in fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emissions per flight.
as of july 2026, lufthansa group has equipped 22 long-haul aircraft across four of its airlines with aeroshark technology.

lufthansa technik has begun testing a next-generation version of its aeroshark surface technology on a short-haul airbus a319 operated by lufthansa city airlines, registered d-abgk, flying between munich and hamburg through february 2027.
the testing is being conducted with partner surventis and features about 70 transparent film patches measuring 20 by 20 centimeters applied to the engine cowlings and fuselage.
the trial aims to monitor material durability and application to guide development for future use on aircraft wings and stabilizers that experience higher aerodynamic loads.
kaan p1 is the first of two new airframes built to carry the main flight test campaign for the fifth-generation fighter program.
p1 and p2 were shown publicly in ankara on february 13, 2026, developed using feedback from demonstrator flights.
the initial p0 demonstrator completed taxi trials in march 2023, flew twice in 2024 reaching 10,000 feet, and was reassigned to ground and system testing.
turkish aerospace ceo mehmet demiroglu stated at the farnborough airshow that p1 could fly within a couple of months and p2 before the end of 2026.
turkish aerospace released footage on july 31, 2026, showing the kaan p1 prototype completing its first low-speed taxi test moving under its own power at its ankara facility.

boeing submitted a new four-year contract offer to a union representing 13,000 engineers and scientists and around 4,000 technical staff.
on july 30, 2026, speea announced that following negotiations, the union will endorse the offer to its members.
speea stated progress was achieved on retirement benefits, flexible/virtual work, mandatory overtime limits, health benefits, and non-boeing labor.

airbus helicopters handed over the first nh90 standard 2 helicopter to the french armament general directorate (dga) at marignane on july 30, 2026.
france has ordered a total of 18 nh90 standard 2 helicopters that will be delivered by mid-2029 for the special forces squadron in pau.
in december 2025, spain joined the program by ordering 31 nh90s in a similar standard.
the 18 aircraft will progressively replace the caracal and cougar helicopters currently being operated by the french army.
the dga transferred the helicopter to french army light aviation (alat) on the same day.
the standard 2 configuration includes the safran euroflir 410 d electro-optical system, a new digital map generator, installation for a third crew member, and enlarged sliding windows.

before the strike began, westjet started grounding parts of its boeing 737 fleet to lessen operational disruption.
boeing 737 and 787 flights are affected, while westjet encore dash 8 q400 flights and partner codeshares continue as scheduled.
cupe local 8125 president alia hussain stated that negotiations continued until the last minute but westjet's offer did not go far enough.
the dispute centers on compensation for ground duties, with westjet offering pay for pre-flight and post-flight duties and a first-year double-digit wage increase.
the strike involves approximately 4,400 cabin crew members and has led to the cancellation of more than 300 westjet flights.
westjet flight attendants officially went on strike on august 2, 2026, after negotiations with cupe local 8125 failed to produce a new agreement.
